body:
The login screen requires https (good) but every connection-layer failure
surfaces as "Couldn't reach the server" (IOException catch-all in
LoginViewModel). An SSLHandshakeException from a self-signed/untrusted cert —
the FIRST thing every self-hoster of dev_tls_server.py or a homelab setup hits
— is indistinguishable from wrong-URL/offline, and there is no path to make it
work: Android 7+ never trusts user-installed CAs by default and the app ships
no networkSecurityConfig.

Fix:
- Catch SSLException distinctly in LoginViewModel.submit() (and surface it in
  sync failure states) with an actionable message ("The server's certificate
  isn't trusted...").
- Add android:networkSecurityConfig trusting user-installed CAs (a deliberate,
  documented choice appropriate for a self-hosted-server app: it only extends
  trust to CAs the device owner explicitly installed; system CAs still work).
- Document the options in android/README.md (proper cert via reverse proxy;
  or install your CA as a user CA).
Files: LoginViewModel.kt, AndroidManifest.xml + res/xml/network_security_config.xml,
android/README.md.
title: Android: self-hosted TLS reality — indistinct error messages, self-signed certs unsupported
